result_text:
Suppliers now carry payment terms in days. The full offline `mvn -q -o test` run passed, including a new test.

- **Model:** `Supplier` has a new `paymentTermsDays` field. I kept the old five-argument constructor, which sets the standard 30 days, so existing callers and tests compile and behave as before.
- **Schema:** `schema.sql` adds a `payment_terms_days` column to `supplier`. It defaults to 30 and must not be negative.
- **Entering and changing terms:** `createSupplier` and `updateSupplier` in `DataStorePart01.java` now write the terms, so you can set them at registration and change them when renegotiated.
- **Where it shows:** the terms come back with every supplier read, in the four places you named:
  - all suppliers by name
  - suppliers of a country
  - suppliers with at least a given rating
  - a single supplier looked up by id
- **Other reports:** the suppliers embedded in purchase suggestions, supplier spending, supplier performance, purchased quantity per supplier and single-supplier categories also read the real terms. Otherwise they would have shown 30 for everyone. These edits are in `DataStorePart02.java`, `DataStorePart03.java` and `DataStorePart09.java`.
- **Test:** `SupplierTest.paymentTermsDefaultToThirtyDaysAndCanBeRenegotiated` covers the default, 45 days then renegotiated to 14, and all four lookups.

I did not touch `DemoScenario`. It still registers suppliers with the default and doesn't print the terms.
